A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FedMosaic framework and DRAKE benchmark, with PQ-LoRA renamed Co-LoRA in v4. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original PFL experiments on DRAKE, HFLB and text-only benchmarks, including comparative results, ablations and adaptation experiments.

after.justification: V4 retains those empirical results and adds rank-heterogeneity, GLUE, privacy-attack and asynchronous-distribution-shift experiments.

M1.justification: The renamed Co-LoRA retains PQ-LoRA's core construction, alignment and training procedure. However, v4 A.24 adds a HETLoRA integration: unequal-rank P/Q modules are padded, aggregated using combined HETLoRA and RELA weights, and truncated for redistribution. This is a limited procedural extension.

E1.justification: V4 adds GLUE tasks covering inference, paraphrase, sentiment and linguistic acceptability (A.26), alongside an explicit text-reconstruction attack scenario using CoLA (A.30). These expand evaluated task requirements. The original DRAKE, HFLB and text-only benchmark coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The original PFL comparator sets are retained. V4 adds a substantive privacy-defense comparison against Clipping + Noise, SVD Truncation, Fisher Information and Orthogonal Projection (Table 39). It also evaluates HETLoRA-integrated versions of PFL comparators in the new unequal-rank experiment (A.24, Table 34).

E3.justification: New protocols include ranks {64,128,256}, Dirichlet partitions with concentration {1,0.5,0.1}, two T5 training budgets, and client-specific task-round schedules (A.24–A.26, A.32). A.30 introduces LAMP reconstruction evaluation using ROUGE-L. A.8 expands compute accounting to include initial alignment; retained accuracy values do not establish reruns under that accounting.

E4.justification: V4 adds gradient-frequency and layer-selection analyses (Figures 21–22), pivot-choice tests (Table 38), privacy-defense component ablations and tradeoffs (Table 39, Figure 25), and a task-relevance analysis (Figure 26). It also broadens cross-model CKA and tests robustness to Dirichlet partitions and asynchronous shifts.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments are averaged over three random seeds with standard deviations reported (Section 6.1). No increase in repeated-run counts or new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark accuracy tables are retained, while v4 adds substantial results under new conditions. For example, Table 36 reports GLUE Self A_last of 78.24±0.14 for FedMosaic versus 62.88±0.36 for SFT with 20 rounds and 50 local steps. Table 15 revises relative compute from 1.098 to 1.161 by including alignment.

T1.justification: V4 A.24 adds mathematical definitions for rank-heterogeneous aggregation, including the normalized combination of HETLoRA and RELA weights (Equations 24–25). Its A/B dimension notation is inconsistent. The original two theorems and their proofs remain unchanged; A.30 supplies empirical privacy tests rather than a new privacy theorem.

C1.justification: Despite the new title and Co-LoRA terminology, the main contributions remain relevance-guided aggregation, dimension-invariant cross-architecture adapters, and DRAKE with task heterogeneity and distribution shifts. The introduction and conclusion retain the personalization, generalization and rapid-adaptation claims.

C2.justification: V4 explains the smaller pivot's stability when larger models arrive (A.29), interprets task-relevance patterns through task groups and shared multi-image inputs (A.31), and discusses overcoming the shared-rank restriction through HETLoRA (A.24). The original limitations concerning other modalities and non-transformer architectures are retained.

D1.justification: V2 promises future release of implementations, benchmarks, splits and baselines; v4 reports availability and provides a repository location. V4 also documents T5 hyperparameters, unequal-rank allocations, attack settings and alignment-cost accounting. Existing core hyperparameters, hardware information and pseudocode are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion distinguishing FedMosaic from prior dual-adapter PFL designs. A.24 positions HETLoRA as complementary, while additional citations support privacy defenses, T5/GLUE and InternLM/InternVL analyses. The established research positioning otherwise remains stable.

P1.justification: V4 changes the title and adapter terminology, rewrites the abstract and problem statement, brings benchmark-category explanations into Section 5, and relocates baseline descriptions to A.6. These are localized revisions within a largely retained document structure.

P2.justification: V4 adds CKA, gradient-cost, privacy and task-relevance visualizations, plus six experimental tables. Figure 2 is redrawn, and v2's appendix sample Figure 21 is redesigned and moved to main-text Figure 6. The DRAKE configuration table and tree are retained with renumbering and label revisions.

improvement.justification: V4 strengthens validation of previously untested design choices through gradient-layer and pivot ablations, asynchronous shifts and direct privacy attacks. More complete compute accounting and documented code/split access also improve the paper. These gains supplement v2's already extensive core evidence. The privacy experiment remains limited to LAMP on CoLA and does not establish a general guarantee, while the new rank-extension exposition contains inconsistent dimension notation.
